title: Chips And Compute: From Research Policy To Fab Conversion
summary: Follow semiconductor policy, research funding, advanced-packaging awards, governance changes, and physical fab milestones without treating any one stage as proof of manufacturing capacity.
current_state_summary: The Published record now reaches from named research and packaging instruments to a Phoenix structural-construction milestone, but the trail remains split across institutions, facilities, utilities, workforce systems, and qualification stages.
current_state: NIST records support a definitive research agreement, three named advanced-packaging awards, and an operating transition for the National Semiconductor Technology Center.
The OpenAI prototype agreement demonstrates how ceiling value and initial obligation must remain separate in compute procurement.
Phoenix records a topping-out milestone for TSMC Fab 3, which is physical progress but not building completion, occupancy, equipment qualification, or production.
APS now identifies TSMC in its service territory, while NNME Southwest identifies a 47-member workforce coordination system across five states.
The U.S. Southwest receiving system still lacks a complete facility-level power, water, wastewater, workforce-outcome, permit, supplier, and operating record.

dependency_stack.current_state: A definitive NIST agreement and final NAPMP awards name instruments, recipients, functions, and maximum funding.
dependency_stack.boundary: An agreement or award does not establish completed work, an operating facility, qualified process, or production output.

dependency_stack.current_state: Commerce says NIST assumed NSTC operations and reopened questions around the Natcast program trail.
dependency_stack.boundary: The action does not supply recipient-by-recipient disposition, executed facility contracts, available funds, or completed research access.

dependency_stack.current_state: METIS and the NAPMP award set expose data, measurement, substrates, equipment, and piloting as separate implementation layers.
dependency_stack.boundary: Beta data infrastructure and award plans do not prove external use, manufacturing validation, commercialization, or industry capacity.

dependency_stack.current_state: TSMC Fab 3 reached topping out in Phoenix while later facilities were described as beginning construction.
dependency_stack.boundary: Topping out is not completion, equipment installation, certificate of occupancy, process qualification, customer acceptance, or production.

dependency_stack.current_state: Arizona now has a named TSMC serving utility, a 47-member regional workforce node, and utility, water, wastewater, construction, and permitting rails for continued review.
dependency_stack.boundary: Service-territory identity and consortium formation do not demonstrate customer capacity, delivered workforce outcomes, corridor-wide readiness, or facility-level sufficiency.

evidence_limits: The Published record does not reconcile the disposition of every NSTC, Natcast, and NAPMP commitment after the operating transition.
No pathway record proves that a named Arizona fab has sufficient electric, water, wastewater, workforce, supplier, or public-infrastructure capacity.
APS's TSMC service-territory statement does not disclose a service agreement, load, infrastructure, energization, consumption, or spare capacity.
NNME Southwest's membership and intended activities do not measure funded delivery, enrollment, completions, placement, retention, vacancies, or supplier outcomes.
Construction milestones cannot stand in for equipment installation, process qualification, customer acceptance, output, yield, or sustained operation.
Prototype-agreement values and research-award ceilings are not equivalent to obligations, outlays, delivered systems, or production capacity.
next_records: Recipient-level NAPMP and NSTC agreement, payment, facility, equipment, staffing, and access records after the NIST operating transition.
TSMC Fab 3 building-completion, inspection, occupancy, equipment-installation, commissioning, qualification, customer, and production records.
TSMC customer-specific electric-service, load, infrastructure, energization, water-service, wastewater, reclaimed-water, and permit records for each Phoenix campus facility.

NNME Southwest agreements, budgets, delivered training capacity, enrollment, completions, credentials, placement, retention, employer demand, supplier openings, and sustained operating-employment records.
